source: Thus, I must go into town to satiate myself. Katherine's stage makeup is good, but it isn't that good.
I don't think she's ever noticed me among the crowd. I keep to myself.
Well, Bernardo-- or Katherine-- is more than a little tormented over others finding out about this.
So you... immediately... ran to... come tell me and everyone else you know?
No! Well, you. I thought you might be able to help Bernardo, for precisely the reason you mentioned.
I'm just trying to find someone Bernardo can talk to.
You've traveled all over and met all kinds of people. Have you ever met anyone like Bernardo?
Putting aside my utter disgust at you for the moment... yes, many a time.
My dear, I have just the thing to cure this forlorn spirit. Allow me to handle this.
May I speak with you?
About you as Katherine.
As I said before, please don't tell anyone anything, and let me handle the matter.
I understand. And I'll heed that. But I'd like you to know something, too.
I also know this might seem sudden, and strange. But I want you to know once more that I have your back.
And that I am, as always, your faithful friend. No matter how you want to be called.
It's been a strange life, this one.
I never meant for you to find out, truth be told.
I thought I could keep the two parts of me separated. As though we were different people.
But the pressure of it felt like I was being ripped in two.
No one can live like that forever.
I'm glad I can be honest with you, Ophelia. Thank you.
Certainly. What about?
I know that you go by both Bernardo and Katherine.
I also know this might seem sudden, and strange. But I want you to know that I have your back.
I-I'm afraid I don't know what you mean. It's...
Please, ah, please pardon me, Ophelia. But I really must go.
Whatever you think you saw, please don't tell anyone.
(Hmm. I don't think it was wise of me to spring the news like that.)
Do you know where Bernardo goes at night?
Is... it bad news?
No. Merely worth sharing.
Bernardo performs in a theater troupe, where he performs as a woman: Katherine.
I often thought... well... er... suspected...
Never mind it.
I must speak to him immediately.
Ahh, I see the news has broken at last. A good secret can only stay hidden so long!
Yes, I've been keeping the good captain's dirty little secret under hat. But really, Lady Ophelia, I was doing him a service.
Can you imagine the fresh hell it would raise if Marcellus and the other guards found out? Or his friends?
If I really wanted to shame Bernardo, I would have told the other men a long time ago.
Who do you think you can trust with something like that, girl? I implore you to find out, both to sate your curiosity and mine.
...The bar?
Ah, no, never mind it. I forgot he'd given up drink a while back. That pious fool. Honestly.
He performs with an amateur theater troupe in town, as a woman. Katherine.
One of those sorts of players?
How did he never... how did I never know?
I wish I had time to discuss this with him, but my ship is about to depart.
Still, sister, I urge you to be silent on this matter.
And he never told me. No. I won't stand for it.
I must speak with him as soon as possible.
Bernardo believes there might be a spy in the castle. What do you know?
Well, there's Guilda and I. The King asked us to sort of keep an eye on Hamlet.
I mean something more nefarious. An attempt by Norway to meddle in Danish affairs, that sort of thing.
Oh. Well, Guilda likes to pretend to be a multinational spy at inns when she's had too much to drink...
It hasn't exactly made us many friends.
But I don't think that's what you mean here. So no, I've not heard anything, but shall let you know if I do.
Me! It's me!
Yes, I'm the Norwegian spy! I just couldn't help but lend myself to Norway's cause.
On account of Prince Fortinbras being so dre-e-e-eamy, and all. I'd kill a hundred men for him!
Guilda, this isn't a make-believe scenario.
Oh. It isn't?
Well, then. That's no fun. I thought we were pretending.
Hmm, speaking of pretending...
Don't forget that once I start hiding, you'll need to invite absolutely everyone to my funeral!
Show me someone who isn't a spy in this castle, and I'll show you a fool or a corpse.
Very funny. But truly--have you seen anything... suspicious?
If I had, that would be our good friend Bernardo's little problem, wouldn't it?
Although, come to think of it...
It's likely nothing. Something odd. I'll speak to Bernardo about it when I can.
Bernardo believes a spy may be hiding in Elsinore. What do you know?
Oh, of course! Ask the dark-skinned outsider what he knows of spies and treachery.
I... I didn't mean it that way, Horatio. I merely wanted to know if you had information I didn't.
My apologies, Ophelia. I'm a bit on edge. I can sense the bluebloods of this castle looking at me sidelong and clutching their bosoms with fear.
Luckily, the good Bernardo believes I'm pure of heart... for now. And as he's running the investigation, his opinion is the only one that matters.
Still, if you haven't spoken to him, perhaps you ought to. Just to set your mind at ease.
Bernardo believes a foreign spy may be embedded in Elsinore. What do you know?
Why must the spy be foreign? Why not someone with hatred of the throne?
Many would see a knife in my lady's back. Many would slit her husbands' throats.
Many people wanted my lady dead, I'm certain, for the simple reason of her station.
But the true threat is under their very noses, in the last place they look.
And who might that be?
My lady listens to nothing I say... but that boy... he will be the end of her. And Claudius, too.
My lady listens to nothing I say... but that boy... he will be the end of her.
Who is to say where the boy goes at night and to whom he speaks? He's friends with that snake-whisperer of a scholar, that Horatio!
What are the two of them doing constantly? That's what I want to know!
Bernardo believes a spy in Elsinore. Have you seen anything amiss?
I... I'm afraid I try not to think about these sorts of things right now, Ophelia.
If you've seen anything amiss...
Then I urge you to go to Captain Bernardo and tell him, of course. That's his profession—not mine.
Of course, my lady.
I've heard the news about a spy in Elsinore. What do you know?
Ah. You've heard of that already? Did Voltemand tell you?
Despite how worrying it may sound, I feel certain the danger to you is very little, my lady.
I don't care about that. I want information. What can you tell me?
It is an ongoing investigation. At the moment, it is up to myself and my men to get to the bottom of it.
I never expected to need to arrest your father, of all people. So this really is a strange and sensitive circumstance.
I never expected to need to arrest Hamlet's schoolmates, of all people. So this really is a strange and sensitive circumstance.
I've been asking all with suspicious information to report it to me. That is—if you think someone knows something about all this...
Tell them I've requested a meeting with them.
I'll interrogate them further. Politely, of course.
My lord, I'd like to discuss the rumors of a spy in Elsinore Castle.
A spy?
Pah hah hah! Wherever did you hear a story like that?
(Ah, right. He hasn't found out about it yet.)
Yes? And what of them?
Have you seen something awry?
If you have cause for suspicion, speak to Captain Bernardo immediately. He has my explicit trust in handling this matter swiftly.
Bernardo's found the traitor. I think that puts an end to the matter for the time being. Don't you?
What news are you talking about? You're making that up, aren't you?
Classic. Your life is so boring, you have to invent some flair.
(Ah, right. No one in the castle knows about the spy yet.)
As much as you do, 'Feely.
I must admit, Claudius's constant paranoia gets tiresome. I don't know how the Queen stands it!
Powerful men can be so odd. Did you hear about the last King of England? Some said he was madder than Hamlet.
He even had his pretty young wife killed. In public! With the way Claudius has been carrying on lately...
Anyhow, isn't it Bernardo's occupation to worry about such things? Bother him, why don't you?
Father, I heard the worrying news about a spy in the castle.
A spy? Where? Who told you?
(Ah. Right. Morning court hasn't happened yet—they don't know.)
I, er, overheard Bernardo discussing it.
I see. I certainly find the notion very interesting, but not substantial as of yet.
You don't think there's a spy going around after all?
Oh... I'm not saying that necessarily, dearest. Everyone's on high alert lately. Suspicions are running high.
I find it odd, but not noteworthy unless some evidence turns up to reinforce this rumor.
Regardless, if you see anything concerning, I urge you to speak with the good guard captain Bernardo about this. He can put your mind at ease.
Hamlet is going to try to overthrow Grace and escape. He intends for you and Guilda to perish.
What? That couldn't be so.
Although, given Hamlet's mood swings as of late...
I suppose it wouldn't be surprising. How can you know this?
He told me himself. He asked that I be ready to escape with him.
Evidently he really has forgotten us.
Thank you for informing us. We'll keep a close watch.
Hamlet is going to try to overthrow Grace and escape. He intends for you and Rosencrantz to perish.
What? How d'you know that?
Y-you think he'd let us die?
But... he's our friend!
This was all supposed to be a relaxing trip. But all of us might die... how's anyone supposed to relax like that?
It's murder on all sides, Ophelia. It's murder soup. Served ice cold!
Even on the open sea, everyone's trying to have everyone else killed.
I felt you ought to know, in the interest of protecting yourself.
Thanks for telling me. Rosie and I will keep a look-out.
So. This plan of yours.
Can you not clear up any misconceptions with Lady Rosencrantz and Lady Guildenstern?
Misconceptions? Ophelia, they were carrying my death warrant.
I can bear no further trust for them.
They seem so... guileless. How could they be plotting your death?
